Log

class Log(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: object

Logging manager for application diagnostics and exceptions.

This singleton class configures a rotating log file handler and provides methods to record informational events, warnings and errors. It also collects system and Python environment data for richer diagnostics.

Parameters:
log_filestr | None, optional

Path to the log file. Default is None, which uses LOG_FILE_PATH.

log_levelint, optional

Logging level of the logger and of the file handler, such as logging.DEBUG or logging.INFO. Default is logging.DEBUG.

Attributes:
LOG_FILE_NAMEstr, class attribute

Default log file name ("tteaapp.log").

LOG_FILE_PATHstr, class attribute

Default log file path, resolved by PathConfig.log when the module is imported.

_instanceLog | None, class attribute

Cached singleton instance.

log_filestr

Path of the log file in use.

loggerlogging.Logger

The "Log" logger that receives all messages.

Methods

get_log()

Retrieve the singleton Log instance.

Write system and Python environment information to the log.

log_error_with_stack(exception, variables=None, traceback_obj=None)

Log exceptions with stack traces and optional context.

log_info(message)

Write an informational message to the log.

log_warning(message)

Write a warning message to the log.

log_error(message)

Write an error message to the log.

Notes

__new__ always returns the same instance, but Python still runs __init__ on every Log(...) call: each call reconfigures the shared instance (file, level and handler). Use get_log() to reuse the instance without reconfiguring it.

On initialization the log directory is created if missing, existing handlers of the "Log" logger are removed to avoid duplicate output, and a RotatingFileHandler is added (10 MiB per file, 5 backups, format "%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s" with dates as %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S). The message "Log instance initialized." is then written at INFO level.

Retrieve the singleton instance of the Log class.

Returns:

The singleton instance of the Log class.

Notes

If no instance exists, a new one is created with default parameters. An existing instance is returned as is, without reconfiguration.

ensure_log_directory_exists()[source]

Create the log file directory if it does not exist.

Notes

Uses os.makedirs on the directory of the absolute path of log_file, creating intermediate directories as needed.

get_system_info()[source]

Retrieve system, hardware and memory information.

Returns:
dict[str, str]

Information keyed by "OS", "OS Version", "Machine", "Processor", "CPU Cores", "Memory Total (GB)", "Memory Used by App (MB)" and "Timestamp".

Notes

Despite the annotation, not every value is a string: "CPU Cores" is the logical core count from psutil (an int, or None if undetermined) and the memory values are floats rounded to 2 decimals. "Memory Total (GB)" is the total physical memory divided by 1024**3; "Memory Used by App (MB)" is the resident set size (RSS) of the current process divided by 1024**2. "Timestamp" uses %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.

get_python_info()[source]

Retrieve Python and installed package information.

Returns:
dict[str, str]

Information keyed by "Python Version" (sys.version), "Python Executable" (sys.executable) and "Installed Packages".

Notes

Installed packages come from importlib.metadata, formatted as "name==version", sorted alphabetically and joined with ", ". If none is found the value is "No packages found".

log_system_info()[source]

Write system and Python environment information to the log.

Notes

Writes a header line followed by each key-value pair of get_system_info() and of get_python_info(), all at INFO level.

log_error_with_stack(exception, variables=None, traceback_obj=None)[source]

Log an error with stack trace and diagnostic context.

Parameters:
exceptionException

The exception to log.

variablesdict[str, Any] | None, optional

Variables to include in the log output. Default is None.

traceback_objAny | None, optional

Traceback object to format. If None, the traceback of the exception currently being handled is used. Default is None.

Notes

Everything is written at ERROR level, in this order:

  1. variables, if given, each value serialized with json.dumps(indent=2, default=str);

  2. the local variables of the caller’s frame (sys._getframe(1)), skipping names that start with __, serialized the same way;

  3. get_system_info() and get_python_info();

  4. str(exception) and the execution stack.

With traceback_obj the stack comes from traceback.format_tb; otherwise from traceback.format_exc, so call it inside the except block. Outside it, format_exc returns "NoneType: None" and that is what gets logged.
